doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Dizzy Gillespie and Jon Faddis as the trumpet standard
summary: He tells trumpet players to study with Jon Faddis for the Dizzy system and calls Dizzy king of the trumpet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: That’s how you get better. You never stop growing, you never stop listening, you never stop learning. You know like I was thinking about the trumpet players. I said they can listen to anybody but the one trumpet player, say other than say Clark, Joe Wilder or Snooky, all the trumpet players I don’t care who you are to this day should be hanging out with Jon Faddis to get the Dizzy Gillespie system. See that’s who they should be checking out. Jon Faddis. Because for me Dizzy still, if there is a king on the trumpet I still got to give Dizzy the edge. Sorry. That’s the way I feel about it. John Birks, you know? Hey man, you know?
